title: Universal semantic error and live learning closure
root_cause: The existing material writeback guard proved that learning, ledger and documentation files existed, but did not verify that the learning contained reusable root-cause, prevention and evidence semantics. That allowed checkbox-style closure to satisfy path presence while carrying weak learning value. During delivery, the same PR branch was also mutated by commits belonging to a different resource-governor obligation, demonstrating that branch identity alone does not protect obligation lineage. The contamination repeated while the PR was still in BUILDING state, confirming that terminal writer ownership must be activated before final reconciliation rather than relying on branch naming or social coordination. A later backend replay exposed a second delivery-learning defect: the regression test was edited from an assumption about a stricter public-visibility rule without first reading the canonical site/website-release-risk.json and lane-website.yml contract. The canonical contract requires public-visibility for fast-fix and high-risk, while normal-risk intentionally omits the sitewide sweep. The incorrect oracle therefore created a false CI failure.
impact: Chats, agents or workflows could technically satisfy closure without enough durable information to prevent recurrence or teach the next worker.
failed_approaches: Treating the presence of a learning file as equivalent to useful learning.
Changing a regression oracle from an inferred safety rule without first reading the canonical runtime/config source of truth.
fix: Extend the central material-writeback guard with semantic validation and bind the same rule into continuity/delivery skills and the universal learning policy.
prevention_rule: Every material candidate must include semantic learning with fingerprint, failure class, evaluation replay, root cause, prevention/regression and evidence. After merge, LIVE_BEWEZEN remains blocked until production readback, outcome evidence and required skill projection are proven by terminal closure. A canonical obligation branch must be bounded by an expected-path allowlist; cross-obligation changed paths trigger fail-closed recovery by rebuilding from the exact current-main base tree plus only the obligation-approved delta before any terminal landing. Before final reconcile/landing, set an explicit TERMINAL_DELIVERY writer lease bound to obligation, PR scope, exact head and exact main epoch; non-owners must DEFER until terminal closure releases the lease. Regression-oracle changes must be SOURCE-OF-TRUTH-FIRST: read the canonical runtime/config contract and workflow at the exact candidate head before changing expected assertions. Never infer a stricter or looser contract from an earlier failing test alone. For the website lane, public-visibility is required for fast-fix and high-risk; normal-risk intentionally uses bounded targeted checks without the sitewide public-visibility sweep.
